cells.tense: You are at the bench right now with the pen, and the build is holding.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Point one person to the route you took through a change you had to make — where you crossed, plainly, once. Then step back; the walking is theirs.
cells.core:
The first structure raised by more than a single pair of hands is going up, and your part is the steady route, not the hurry. When the last step isn't visible, you lay the one you can see solidly, and the next one shows itself. Practice is feeding the work rather than eating it.

The place refinement starts to press is when it corrects and rushes the next step instead of laying it. Naming the passage the way you actually crossed it, once, is the whole of what you owe anyone. Then the move belongs to them, and you step back to your own bench, no force in it. Directions handed over plainly, once, is what this balance is free to feed next.
cells.sheetLine: You can show the route you crossed, then let it be theirs.
cells.verb: build something new out of what the clearing left, by hand, alongside others
cells.place: the open space made by letting go of what no longer serves

cells.tense: The build is being rushed forward faster than the ground under it has settled.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Choose a shared thing you're about to rebuild or push past. Go into it as it actually is now, drop the version you rehearsed, and stay until you hear someone still in it.
cells.core:
The structure is rising ahead of ground that hasn't been cleared, and bracing at something unwritable is doing the building. Each dark patch gets a wall raised over it, and the walls weigh more than the road does. What hasn't been let go of is being built around rather than released, and the people near it carry what they didn't ask for.

What's thin here isn't restraint — it's closeness: standing within something shared while it's alive, alongside the people it holds. Go deeper than is comfortable into a thing that still connects you, and leave the hollow version behind. The direction you're defending has people in it, and they haven't been asked. Afterwards, fewer things get raised, and the ones that do hold.
cells.sheetLine: You're raising walls over ground you haven't cleared yet.
cells.verb: build something new out of what the clearing left, by hand, alongside others
cells.place: the open space made by letting go of what no longer serves

cells.tense: The clearing already happened, and nothing has been built on it since.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Settle a build you've been circling before tonight, make the first move today, and tell nobody ahead of it.
cells.core:
The ground is cleared and nothing is standing on it. You build only where the way is already lit, which at this point means nothing gets built at all, and the strength is right there in your hands, going unused. Letting go opened the space; waiting inside it has taken over the whole stance. Even now, making the call and carrying it through is open to you.

What serves what it organizes doesn't need announcing. Settle the shape of a thing and take the first move today — no pitch, no permission, no account owed. Movement from real engagement gives the direction, and the next lit stretch shows after the step, not before. That is how a foundation starts.

cells.tense: You keep one heading steady for everyone around you and call it simply carrying on.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Find a direction you chose yourself this month, where no pressure sits on it. Hold that heading once when it's pushed, then notice what held you.
cells.core:
The heading is being kept, reliably, through stretches nobody else can see the far side of. When it's contested you keep it, and your account of it has you carrying on. The direction you picked is yours, and you talk about it as ground rather than stance.

Go back before it was for anyone else: what you moved on because it felt real, before there was anything to defend. That earlier response is still running beneath everything you hold now. Name the direction and keep it once, plainly, when it's pushed, and let what it rested on come into view. The choice gets its name back, and the same steadiness from here is chosen, not inherited.
cells.sheetLine: That heading is your choice, and it reads like carrying on.
